record.what_it_does: Chat platform for communities; API for bots, messaging, guilds, and OAuth2 user integrations.
record.auth_notes: Bot token for bot actions in guilds the bot was added to. OAuth2 (authorization code, with PKCE; implicit and client credentials also supported) for acting as a user, with limited scopes. A multi-user toolkit would use OAuth2 for identity and guild install, then act via the bot token. User-level message read/send is not offered through OAuth2, and self-botting with user tokens is against the ToS.
record.access_notes: Anyone can create an app and bot for free in the Developer Portal. Some OAuth scopes, such as dm_channels.read and voice, need Discord approval. Bots in 100+ guilds need verification, and privileged intents such as Message Content need approval at that scale (I know this from prior knowledge; the page I fetched didn't cover it).
record.api_breadth_notes: REST covers channels, messages, guilds, members, roles, threads, webhooks, interactions, application commands, users, and more. The Gateway websocket delivers real-time events.
record.mcp_notes: Many community servers exist, e.g. SaseQ/discord-mcp. A search result claimed a docs-search-only official server at docs.discord.com/mcp. My fetch of that URL returned HTTP 405 (it may be a POST-only endpoint), so I couldn't confirm it. It would not cover messaging anyway.
record.blocker_notes: The API is open and free, but it is bot-centric. Acting as an end user is limited, because OAuth2 doesn't give user-level message read/send. Gated scopes, bot verification beyond 100 guilds, and privileged intents add review. Webhook events are limited and need a public endpoint. The Gateway is needed for real-time triggers.

evidence.quote: We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials
Some scopes require approval from Discord to use.
Webhook events are one-way events sent to your app over HTTP to notify you when an event occurred.
Verified bots do not have a maximum number of guilds.

record.needs_human: Confirm whether Discord now hosts an official MCP server at docs.discord.com/mcp (docs search only?). Also confirm current verification and privileged-intent requirements, which I didn't see on a fetched page.
